de.hsub: Specialty Coffee und Frühstück den ganzen Tag, in dem Haus, in dem 1860 Soprons erstes Fotoatelier eröffnete.
de.hazP1: Sándor Tiefbrunner eröffnete 1860 in diesem Haus Soprons erstes Fotoatelier, einen Salon für Fotografie und Glas. Hier entstanden Porträts, Landschaften und Stereobilder.

de.hhP: Várkerület 96. Fotoatelier ab 1860, Café seit Dezember 2015.
de.hh1P: Sándor Tiefbrunner eröffnete 1860 in diesem Haus Soprons erstes Fotoatelier, einen Salon für Fotografie und Glas. Sein Flugblatt warb auf Deutsch für das Atelier, damals unter der Adresse Grabenrunde 93: so hieß der Várkerület damals.
de.hhForras: Tiefbrunners Flugblatt, zitiert von József Hárs: Die Geschichte der Fotografie in Sopron 1840–1957 (1984, ungarisch).
de.hh2P: Es war Atelier und Labor: Hier entstanden Porträts, Landschaften, plastische und räumliche Objekte sowie Stereobilder. Ein Stereobild besteht aus zwei fast gleichen Fotos, die sich beim Betrachten zu einem räumlichen Bild verbinden.
de.hh3P: An der Wand hinter der Theke steht Robert Capas schwarze Silhouette mit Filmkamera. Capa wurde 1913 in Budapest als Endre Friedmann geboren und wurde einer der bekanntesten Fotoreporter des 20. Jahrhunderts. Daneben der ihm zugeschriebene Satz: „It’s not enough to have talent, you also have to be Hungarian.“
de.ido1: Sándor Tiefbrunner eröffnet im Haus Soprons erstes Fotoatelier.
de.ido2: Im Dezember, an einem ruhigen Tag vor Silvester, eröffnet das Kultúrpresszó.
de.ido3: Am 1. Mai eröffnet unser zweites Café, das Botanik, im Botanischen Garten.
de.bbP: Café im Botanischen Garten der Universität Sopron, im Glashaus des Ligneum. Wir sind seit dem 1. Mai 2025 hier.
de.bb1P: Wir kochen denselben Kaffee wie am Várkerület, geröstet von 42 Coffee. Durch die Glaswände sehen Sie die Bäume des Botanischen Gartens.
de.bbM: Am Wochenende haben wir nur bei Veranstaltungen geöffnet, diese kündigen wir auf Instagram an.

en.altHero: Kultúrpresszó’s terrace in the evening on Várkerület, string lights glowing on the facade
en.h1: A café on Várkerület in Sopron
en.hsub: Specialty coffee and all-day breakfast in the building where Sopron’s first photo studio opened in 1860.
en.hazP1: In 1860 Sándor Tiefbrunner opened Sopron’s first photo studio in this building, a salon for photography and glass. Portraits, landscapes and stereo pictures were made here.
en.hazP2: In December 2015, on a quiet day before New Year’s Eve, we opened our café in the same place.
en.capaCap: Robert Capa behind the bar, with his line on the wall: “It’s not enough to have talent, you also have to be Hungarian.”
en.kaveP: Our blend is roasted for us by 42 Coffee: half Ethiopian Heirloom, half Brazilian Yellow Bourbon, both natural process.
en.kaveM: Ask at the bar which guest coffee we are pouring right now.
en.etelP: All-day breakfast, sandwiches and bagels, spreads in vegan versions too. Cakes in paleo, gluten-free and vegan versions.
en.etlapM: The coffee prices come from our menu in the café. You will find the full menu and the cakes of the day at the bar.
en.teraszP: In good weather we sit outside in front of the building, and in the evening the string lights glow above the door. Click the photo and we will develop it.
en.gepAria: Take a picture of the terrace
en.g1: The interior, the mural at the back
en.g5: A latte on the Persian rug
en.progP: We host mini concerts, book launches and unusual history and Hungarian lessons, and you can celebrate your birthday with us too. During SopronFest our terrace is a venue as well.
en.progUres: We announce the next events on Instagram.
en.botP: Since 1 May 2025 we have also been making coffee in the University of Sopron’s Botanical Garden, in the glass building of the Ligneum. Weekdays 8:30–16:00, at weekends during events.
en.infoM: There is wifi, you can pay by card, and children and dogs are welcome.
en.terkepP: The map is a Google service, Google may set cookies when it loads.
en.introS3: People have taken photographs in this house since 1860.

en.hhP: Várkerület 96. A photo studio from 1860, a café since December 2015.
en.hh1P: In 1860 Sándor Tiefbrunner opened Sopron’s first photo studio in this building, a salon for photography and glass. His flyer advertised the studio in German, at the address Grabenrunde 93: that was the name of Várkerület at the time.
en.hhForras: Tiefbrunner’s flyer, quoted by József Hárs: The history of photography in Sopron 1840–1957 (1984, in Hungarian).
en.hh2P: It was a studio and a laboratory: portraits, landscapes, sculptural and three-dimensional objects and stereo pictures were made here. A stereo picture is two almost identical photos that merge into one three-dimensional image for the viewer.
en.hh3P: On the wall behind the bar stands Robert Capa’s black silhouette with a film camera. Capa was born in Budapest in 1913 as Endre Friedmann and became one of the best-known photojournalists of the 20th century. Next to him is the line attributed to him: “It’s not enough to have talent, you also have to be Hungarian.”
en.ido1: Sándor Tiefbrunner opens Sopron’s first photo studio in the building.
en.ido2: In December, on a quiet day before New Year’s Eve, Kultúrpresszó opens.
en.ido3: On 1 May our second café, Botanik, opens in the Botanical Garden.
en.bbP: A café in the University of Sopron’s Botanical Garden, in the glass building of the Ligneum. We have been here since 1 May 2025.
en.bb1P: We make the same coffee as on Várkerület, roasted by 42 Coffee. Through the glass walls you look out at the trees of the botanical garden.
en.bbM: At weekends we only open during events, which we announce on Instagram.
